Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with clear sections (Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Results, Discussion, Conclusion). Hypotheses H-E1 and H-M1 are explicitly defined, variance decomposition formulas are provided, and results are presented in tables with thresholds and pass/fail status. Minor issues include occasional references to unavailable full zoo size (~30k models) and a few code comments that are not reflected in the main text.

Novelty.justification: The work extends scalar accuracy prediction (Unterthiner et al., SANE) to structured class-wise accuracy vectors, which is a logical next step. The positive existence result (67.6% residual variance) combined with the negative mechanism result on simple statistics is informative. However, the core ideas build directly on prior weight-space learning literature without introducing fundamentally new architectures or theoretical bounds.

Soundness.justification: H-E1 is validated on real Small CNN Zoo data (193 models) with residual ratio 0.676 > 0.05 threshold. H-M1 correctly fails (ΔR² = -0.20) using 25 handcrafted features and Ridge regression. Code executes the described pipeline (model loading, inference on CIFAR-10, variance analysis, ridge probe) and produces matching numerical results. Limitations include small sample size, single architecture family, and reliance on a PoC subset in one experiment log, but the reported metrics are internally consistent.

Significance.justification: The paper addresses a genuine gap—predicting behavioral profiles rather than scalar accuracy—from weights. The negative result on simple statistics usefully motivates learned representations (Neural Functionals, SANE). Impact is tempered by the narrow scope (one zoo, one feature set, under-trained models with 18.7% mean accuracy) and lack of cross-architecture or cross-dataset validation.

strengths: Clear hypothesis-driven structure with explicit thresholds and pass/fail criteria
Empirical validation of behavioral variance existence on real model-zoo data
weaknesses: Mechanism test uses only simple statistics and yields negative result without exploring stronger baselines
Limited to a single small zoo and architecture family with no cross-dataset validation
